_comment: Hand-curated names and notes for what the game leaves numbered. Never generated; see CLAUDE.md.

8.name: Laser
8.note: A beam between two cells, named in the record's own fields rather than drawn between blocks that happen to line up. It runs on one axis on all 117 in the game, and no block ever stands between its ends. One field gives that axis and another says whether it starts lit. Its ends carry the emitter blocks, and 61 of the 234 sit on cells the lattice leaves empty, which is the game placing geometry a level's own grid does not.

666.name: Camera
666.note: The record every level ends with, and the one entity that stands on no cell: where its position would be, the disc writes three 0xFFFF. It carries a cell for the camera to look at, two angles, and a number that is 99 on 218 of the 230 levels and lower on the other twelve, which reads as the level's time. It draws as the look-at ring rather than as an object marker.

0/0.name: Blue coin
0/0.note: 1206 placed across 159 levels, the game's most numerous object. Absent from LEVEL 1, where no blue coin appears; it starts turning up from LEVEL 3.

0/7.name: Exit
0/7.note: The exit of LEVEL 1 and LEVEL 2 stands on the cell the map draws this on. Exactly one in each of 122 levels and never two; what the other 108 levels leave for is not yet read.

0/30.name: Start
0/30.note: The block the ball starts on, in LEVEL 1 and LEVEL 2, and exactly one in each of 182 levels and never two. The 48 without one are not yet understood.

0/31.name: Key
0/31.note: One to four a level and never more: 69 levels with one, 51 with more. Collecting every key is what turns the exit from red to green. LEVEL 1's and LEVEL 2's are on the cells the map draws them on.

0/37.name: Bronze coin
0/37.note: 1044 placed across 155 levels, up to 45 in one. LEVEL 1 holds exactly two and LEVEL 2 six, and the game shows exactly that many bronze coins in each, on the cells the map draws them on.

0/46.name: Fruit
0/46.note: The fruit of LEVEL 1 and LEVEL 2 stands on the cell the map draws this on. Exactly one in each of 59 levels and never two; which fruit stands in it is not in the level, and the game carries an uncollected fruit forward, so the choice is progress rather than data.

8/0.name: Red laser
8/0.note: Seen in OBJ LEVEL: the vertical beam from the floating block to the floor, red at both ends and off until something turns it on. Every one of the nine in the game starts dark.

8/1.name: Green laser
8/1.note: Seen in OBJ LEVEL: the beam between the two floating blocks, green at both ends and lit. Colour is read as the type's rather than the start-state flag's; LEVEL 109 has four of these that start dark and settles which.

/HELL/HELL.PAK#18.note: 160 of its 178 blocks are not part of the level at all. They lie flat on z=32, the floor of the lattice and 22 blocks below the playable structure, spelling VERY WELL DONE in block letters six blocks tall.

/HILLS/HILLS.PAK#19.note: The developer object catalogue, shipped unchanged in nine of the ten worlds and never reached in play. One of nearly every object in the game stands on a flat floor: walk it in an emulator and each one names itself. `tools/kula_objlevel.py` writes the floor plan, and `tools/kula_warp.py` writes a disc copy that reaches it.
